places.name: Raamses
places.note: OpenBible.info has no place of this spelling, so TIPNR's own position, 30 km from Rameses, was drawn; it is the same city.

places.name: Pi-hahiroth
places.note: The camp before the crossing, at the foot of Wadi Watir, after Ron Wyatt and Lennart Möller (The Exodus Case). OpenStreetMap's Nuweiba al-Muzayna.

locations.label: Nuweiba beach, at the mouth of Wadi Watir

places.name: Baal-zephon
places.note: Saraf al-Bal, across the gulf from Nuweiba, after Möller. No gazetteer gives it; the position is the Saudi shore opposite Nuweiba, a little inland.

places.name: Red Sea
places.note: The sea crossed, the Gulf of Aqaba between Nuweiba and Saraf al-Bal, after Wyatt and Möller. OpenBible.info's matching picked the Way of the Red Sea, a road.

locations.label: Gulf of Aqaba, crossed from Nuweiba to Saraf al-Bal

places.name: Marah
places.note: Three days into the wilderness from the crossing (Exodus 15:22-23). The reading gives no site; estimated halfway between Baal-zephon, where the crossing came ashore, and Elim.

places.name: Elim
places.note: The twelve springs of al-Bad', after Möller. OpenStreetMap's Maghair Shuaib.

places.name: Sin
places.note: The wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai (Exodus 16:1). The reading gives no site; estimated a quarter of the way from Elim to Rephidim.

places.name: Dophkah
places.note: After the wilderness of Sin (Numbers 33:12). The reading gives no site; estimated halfway from Elim to Rephidim.

locations.label: between the wilderness of Sin and Alush (estimated)

places.name: Alush
places.note: The last camp before Rephidim (Numbers 33:13-14). The reading gives no site; estimated three quarters of the way from Elim to Rephidim.

places.name: Rephidim
places.note: By the split rock west of Jabal al-Lawz, the position its proponents give (28°43'31.35"N 35°14'15.36"E, as cited by bible.ca).

locations.label: the split rock, west of Jabal al-Lawz

places.name: Massah
places.note: Where the people tested Yahweh at Rephidim (Exodus 17:7), so by the split rock with it. OpenBible.info's follows the traditional Rephidim in the Sinai peninsula.

locations.label: another name for Rephidim: the split rock, west of Jabal al-Lawz

places.name: Meribah
places.note: The Meribah of Rephidim (Exodus 17:7), not that of Kadesh (Numbers 20:13), which TIPNR keeps apart. By the split rock with Rephidim.

locations.label: another name for Rephidim: the split rock, west of Jabal al-Lawz

places.name: Sinai
places.note: Mount Sinai, and Horeb, which TIPNR makes the same record, as Jabal al-Lawz in Midian, after Ron Wyatt, Bob Cornuke and Lennart Möller. OpenBible.info's position for it.

places.name: Sinai Wilderness
places.note: The wilderness about the mountain, so about Jabal al-Lawz.

places.name: Paran Mount
places.note: Mount Paran, from which Yahweh shone forth with Sinai and Seir (Deuteronomy 33:2; Habakkuk 3:3), taken as another name for Mount Sinai, as OpenBible.info's likeliest identification also takes it: so Jabal al-Lawz.

locations.label: another name for Mount Sinai: Jabal al-Lawz, in Midian

places.name: Taberah
places.note: Where the fire burned on the way from Sinai, by Kibroth-hattaavah (Numbers 11:1-3, 34). The reading gives no site; estimated with Kibroth-hattaavah.

places.name: Kibroth-hattaavah
places.note: The first camp after Sinai (Numbers 33:16). The reading gives no site; estimated a third of the way from Jabal al-Lawz to Kadesh at Petra. OpenBible.info's is on the traditional route through the Sinai peninsula.

places.name: Hazeroth
places.note: After Kibroth-hattaavah (Numbers 11:35; 33:17). The reading gives no site; estimated two thirds of the way from Jabal al-Lawz to Kadesh at Petra. OpenBible.info's is on the traditional route through the Sinai peninsula.

places.name: Kadesh
places.note: Kadesh, where Israel came to the border of Edom (Numbers 20:16) and Miriam died, as Petra: the Targums call Kadesh Reqem, Josephus Petra's old name, and Eusebius places Kadesh by Petra; Wadi Musa's spring is held to be where Moses struck the rock, and Aaron's tomb on Jebel Harun overlooks it. Kadesh-barnea, which TIPNR gives the same record, is split from it (see splits).

places.name: Hor Mount
places.note: Mount Hor, where Aaron died on the border of Edom (Numbers 20:22-28), as Jebel Harun above Petra, where his tomb is shown, after Josephus. TIPNR's own position; OpenBible.info puts Har Zin first.
places.summary:
A location first mentioned at Num.20.22
only referred to as Hor Mount (הֹר).

locations.label: Jebel Harun (Jebel Nebi Harun), above Petra

places.name: Sodom
places.note: Bab edh-Dhra, after Joel Kramer (Expedition Bible, 'Sodom burned, Zoar did NOT'), with Walter Rast and Thomas Schaub's survey of the five Early Bronze sites south-east of the Dead Sea. Wikipedia's position; OpenBible.info's is a kilometre off the site.

places.name: Gomorrah
places.note: Numeira, after Kramer. Wikipedia's position.

places.name: Admah
places.note: Feifa, after Kramer. OpenBible.info's position for it.

places.name: Zeboiim
places.note: Khanazir, after Kramer. OpenBible.info's position for it.

places.name: Zoar
places.note: The town spared, at es-Safi, where the Madaba map puts it, after Kramer: Tell esh-Sheikh 'Isa, OpenBible.info's position. With it, Lot's cave (Gen 19:30), which has no record of its own: the cave and Byzantine church of Saint Lot at Deir 'Ain 'Abata above es-Safi, excavated by Konstantinos Politis; OpenStreetMap's position.

locations.label: Lot's cave (Deir 'Ain 'Abata), where Lot fled from Zoar

places.name: Ephraim
places.note: Working identification near et-Taiyibeh, northeast of Jerusalem and beside the wilderness, fitting John 11:54 after Bethany. The identification is uncertain; this point is an estimate, not a surveyed Gospel site.

places.name: Gerasa
places.note: The Gospel country of the Gerasenes/Gadarenes/Gergesenes is represented near Kursi on the eastern lakeshore: landing, tombs and a steep descent into the lake (Mark 5:1-20). This estimates the encounter district, not the inland city of Jerash; the textual names and exact landing are disputed.

places.name: Judean baptizing countryside
places.note: Estimated in the lower Jordan countryside in Judea after Jerusalem (John 3:22), before the journey through Samaria (4:3-5). Aenon is John's location, not a recorded stop by Jesus.

places.name: Solitary place near Capernaum
places.note: Estimated on the outskirts of Capernaum: Jesus leaves the town to pray before visiting neighbouring towns (Mark 1:35-39).

places.name: Galilean teaching hillside
places.note: A working site on the slopes northwest of the lake, between the lakeside ministry and Capernaum (Matthew 4:23-5:1; 8:5; Luke 6:12-7:1). The mountain and level place are unnamed; their identification as one occasion is a harmony choice.

places.name: Solitary place near Bethsaida
places.note: Estimated by the northeastern lakeshore near Bethsaida (Luke 9:10), with open ground for the five thousand and departure by boat (Mark 6:32-45). Not a claim that the feeding occurred in the town.

places.name: Hillside above the eastern lakeshore
places.note: Estimated on the lake-facing Decapolis slopes, following the return through Sidon and the Decapolis (Mark 7:31-8:10; Matthew 15:29-39). The healing and feeding site is unnamed.

places.name: Mountain of the transfiguration
places.note: Working estimate on the southern Hermon slopes after Caesarea Philippi and before the return through Galilee (Mark 8:27-9:33). Neither Hermon nor Tabor is named in the accounts; this is a route-based choice, not an identification of the mountain.

places.name: Samaritan village on the Jerusalem road
places.note: Estimated near the northern entrance to Samaria on a southbound route from Galilee (Luke 9:51-56). The village is unnamed and the disciples move on to another village.

locations.label: Samaritan village on the Jerusalem road (estimated)

places.name: Border country of Samaria and Galilee
places.note: Estimated near the Dothan/Jenin corridor on the Samaria-Galilee border (Luke 17:11-19). Linking this journey to the withdrawal to Ephraim is Robertson's reconstruction, not an explicit connection in John.

locations.label: Border country of Samaria and Galilee (estimated)

places.name: Beyond-Jordan teaching district
places.note: Estimated in the Jordan valley east of the river, before crossing toward Jericho (Mark 10:1,46; Matthew 19:1;20:29). The towns in this teaching journey are unnamed.

places.name: Upper room
places.note: Traditional southwestern-hill vicinity used as a working estimate for the unnamed furnished upper room (Mark 14:12-17; Luke 22:7-14). The surviving Cenacle building is later.

places.name: House of Annas
places.note: Estimated in the affluent Upper City, near the high-priestly quarter, for John 18:13-24. No house of Annas has been securely identified.

places.name: House of Caiaphas
places.note: Working estimate on the southeastern edge of the Upper City, near the traditional high-priestly site. Matthew 26:57 names the host, not the street or building; this identification is uncertain.

places.name: Council meeting place
places.note: Estimated in the Upper City near the high-priestly residences for the morning council (Luke 22:66). The Gospel does not identify its chamber; no route into the Temple precinct is asserted.

places.name: Pilate's praetorium
places.note: Herod's western palace is the working identification of the governor's headquarters (John 18:28-19:16; Mark 15:16). The Antonia fortress is an alternative tradition. The exact trial courtyard is uncertain.

places.name: Herod Antipas' Jerusalem lodging
places.note: Estimated at the traditional Hasmonean-palace area in the Upper City for Luke 23:7-12. His presence in Jerusalem is explicit; his lodging is not named.

places.name: Temple precinct
places.note: Approximate point within the Herodian Temple precinct, used for Gospel events explicitly in the temple. The precinct is geographically secure; an event's exact position within it is usually unknown.

places.name: Solomon's portico
places.note: Estimated along the eastern portico of the Temple precinct, where John 10:23 places Jesus at Dedication. The exact extent and event position are reconstructed.

places.name: Temple treasury
places.note: Working estimate by the Court of Women east of the sanctuary for Mark 12:41-44 and John 8:20. Interior court geometry and the precise collection point are reconstructed.

places.name: Garden tomb near Golgotha
places.note: Working identification in the Holy Sepulchre precinct, adjacent to the traditional Golgotha site (John 19:41-42). The exact burial identification is disputed; the modern Garden Tomb is a separate alternative.

places.name: Mount of Olives toward Bethany
places.note: Estimated on the eastern side of the Mount of Olives toward Bethany (Luke 24:50-51; Acts 1:9-12), not a claim for an exact footprint or chapel site.

places.name: Mountain in Galilee
places.note: A working estimate on the familiar northwestern Galilean hills for Matthew 28:16-20. The appointed mountain is unnamed; using the teaching-hillside vicinity does not identify the two mountains.

places.name: Shore of the Sea of Tiberias
places.note: Estimated on the northwestern lakeshore near the disciples' Galilean base for John 21. The text names the sea, not the beach; this follows the traditional Tabgha vicinity as a working choice.

locations.label: Shore of the Sea of Tiberias (estimated)

places.name: Refuge in Egypt
places.note: A broad working anchor in the eastern Nile delta, reachable from Judea along the coastal corridor (Matthew 2:13-21). The Gospel gives no Egyptian town or internal itinerary; this is a regional guess, not evidence for a particular residence.

places.name: Galilean circuit near Capernaum
places.note: A working anchor west of Capernaum for unnamed towns and villages in the Galilean ministry. The circuit covers a region: this point is not a recovered stop or proof that all episodes occurred in the same town.

places.name: Judean teaching journey
places.note: A working anchor north of Jerusalem for the unnamed villages of Luke's teaching journey. Placement in the later Judean ministry follows Robertson's harmony; the exact towns and dates are not supplied by Luke.

places.name: Fig tree on the Bethany road
places.note: Estimated along the Bethany-to-Jerusalem approach on the Mount of Olives (Mark 11:12-14,20). The tree's actual site is unknown.

locations.label: Fig tree on the Bethany road (estimated)

places.name: Wilderness of the temptations
places.note: Working estimate in the Jordan-valley wilderness near the baptism, following Haqor's existing reading. Matthew 4:1 and Luke 4:1 do not name Beth-arabah or an exact location.

places.name: Pinnacle of the temple
places.note: Working estimate at the southwest corner of the Temple platform, retaining Haqor's existing interpretation. Matthew 4:5 and Luke 4:9 do not identify a corner; the southeast corner is another proposal.

places.name: High mountain of the temptations
places.note: Working estimate near Pisgah, retaining Haqor's existing typological reading. Matthew 4:8 does not name the mountain. This is conjectural, not evidence that Jesus visited the identified summit.

places.name: Emmaus
places.note: El Qubeibeh is the working estimate, chosen for the approximately sixty-stadia distance of Luke 24:13 and return toward Jerusalem. Qalunya and Nicopolis remain alternatives; the text and site identification are disputed. Compare https://www.custodia.org/en/sanctuaries/emmaus-el-qubeibeh/ and https://www.openbible.info/geo/ancient/ae7274b/emmaus . The chosen point is rounded from OpenBible's El Qubeibeh coordinates.

splits.from_summary:
A location first mentioned at Gen.14.7
referred to as Kadesh (קָדֵשׁ), or En-mishpat (עֵין מִשְׁפָּט).
splits.name: Kadesh-barnea
splits.summary:
A location first mentioned at Gen.16.14
referred to as Kadesh-barnea (קָדֵשׁ בַּרְנֵעַ), or Kadesh (קָדֵשׁ) in the Negev, or Kedesh (קֶ֫דֶשׁ).
splits.note: Kadesh-barnea, on the southern border of the land (Numbers 34:4; Joshua 15:3), kept apart from the Kadesh of Edom's border, which Haqor places at Petra. The verses that call it Kadesh-barnea, with the Negev's Kadesh of Abraham and Hagar (Genesis 16:14; 20:1) and Judah's Kedesh (Joshua 15:23); OpenBible.info places it, at Ain el-Qudeirat.
